Cyclic covers and toroidal embeddings

Florin Ambro Address: Institute of Mathematics “Simion Stoilow” of the Romanian Academy
P.O. BOX 1-764, RO-014700 Bucharest
Romania. Email address: florin.ambro@imar.ro
Abstract.

We present an improved version of the cyclic covering trick, which works inside the category of toroidal embeddings.

11footnotetext: This work was supported by a grant of the Romanian National Authority for Scientific Research, CNCS - UEFISCDI, project number PN-II-RU-TE-2011-3-0097. 22footnotetext: 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification. Primary: 14E20; Secondary: 14F17.

Introduction

Cyclic covers are a useful tool in algebraic geometry. The simplest example is the field extension

K⊂K⁡(φn)K\subset K(\sqrt[n]{\varphi})

obtained by adjoining to a field the root of an element. For example, the equation tn−φ​∏izimit^{n}-\varphi\prod_{i}z_{i}^{m_{i}} over KK simplifies to tn−∏izimit^{n}-\prod_{i}z_{i}^{m_{i}} over K⁡(φn)K(\sqrt[n]{\varphi}).

In classical algebraic geometry, cyclic covers were used to construct new examples from known ones. Given a complex projective variety XX, a torsion line bundle LL over XX induces canonically an étale cyclic Galois covering π:X′→X\pi\colon X^{\prime}\to X such that π∗​L\pi^{*}L becomes trivial. If LL has torsion index rr and s∈Γ⁡(X,Lr)s\in\Gamma(X,L^{r}) is nowhere zero, the covering can be constructed as the rr-th root of ss (as in the function field case, the pullback of ss becomes an rr-th power of a section of the pullback of LL). We may denote it by π:X⁡[sr]→X\pi\colon X[\sqrt[r]{s}]\to X. The isomorphism class of π\pi does not depend on the choice of ss, since XX being compact, every two nowhere zero sections differ by a non-zero constant.

Many invariants of X′X^{\prime} can be read off those of XX, but with coefficients in negative powers of LL. For example,

π∗ΩpX′=⊕i=0r−1ΩpX⊗L−i.\pi_{*}\Omega^{p}_{X^{\prime}}=\oplus_{i=0}^{r-1}\Omega^{p}_{X}\otimes L^{-i}.

So one may construct manifolds with prescribed invariants by taking roots of torsion line bundles on known manifolds. The process may be reversed: known statements on the invariants of X′X^{\prime} translate into similar statements on XX, twisted by negative powers of LL. For example, the Kähler differential of X′X^{\prime} decomposes into integrable flat connections on L−iL^{-i}, so that ⊕i=0r−1ΩX∙(L−i)\oplus_{i=0}^{r-1}\Omega^{\bullet}_{X}(L^{-i}) is the Hodge complex π∗​ΩX′∙\pi_{*}\Omega^{\bullet}_{X^{\prime}} on XX. In particular, the E1E_{1}-degeneration for (ΩX′∙,F)(\Omega^{\bullet}_{X^{\prime}},F) translates into the E1E_{1}-degeneration for (ΩX′∙​(L−i),F)(\Omega^{\bullet}_{X^{\prime}}(L^{-i}),F), for every ii. This exchange of information between the total and base space of a cyclic cover is called the cyclic covering trick (cf. sections 1 and 2 of [6] for example).

The range of applications of the cyclic covering trick extends dramatically if ss is allowed to have zeros. In this case ss is a non-zero global section of the nn-th power of some line bundle LL on XX. The nn-th root of ss is defined just as above. We obtain for example the same formula

π∗𝒪X⁡[sn]=⊕i=0n−1L−i.\pi_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X[\sqrt[n]{s}]}=\oplus_{i=0}^{n-1}L^{-i}.

The morphism π\pi is still cyclic Galois and flat, but it ramifies over the zero locus of ss. The total space X⁡[sn]X[\sqrt[n]{s}] may be disconnected (even if ss vanishes nowhere), it may have several irreducible components, and it may even have singularites over the zero locus of ss. These singularities are partially resolved by the normalization X¯​[sn]→X​[sn]\bar{X}[\sqrt[n]{s}]\to X[\sqrt[n]{s}]. The induced morphism π¯:X¯​[sn]→X\bar{\pi}\colon\bar{X}[\sqrt[n]{s}]\to X is cyclic Galois and flat, and one computes

π¯∗𝒪X¯​[sn]=⊕i=0n−1L−i(⌊inZ(s)⌋).\bar{\pi}_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{\bar{X}[\sqrt[n]{s}]}=\oplus_{i=0}^{n-1}L^{-i}(\lfloor\frac{i}{n}Z(s)\rfloor).

Here Z⁡(s)Z(s) is the effective Cartier divisor cut out by ss, and the round down of the ℚ{\mathbb{Q}}-divisor in​Z​(s)\frac{i}{n}Z(s) is defined componentwise. If Supp⁡Z⁡(s)\operatorname{Supp}Z(s) has no singularities, then X¯​[sn]\bar{X}[\sqrt[n]{s}] has no singularities. Differential forms or vector fields on X¯​[sn]\bar{X}[\sqrt[n]{s}] are computed in terms of X,LX,L, and the ℚ{\mathbb{Q}}-divisor 1n​Z​(s)\frac{1}{n}Z(s). For example

π¯∗ΩX¯​[sn]p=⊕i=0n−1ΩXp(logSupp{inZ(s)})⊗L−i(⌊inZ(s)⌋),\bar{\pi}_{*}\Omega^{p}_{\bar{X}[\sqrt[n]{s}]}=\oplus_{i=0}^{n-1}\Omega^{p}_{X}(\log\operatorname{Supp}\{\frac{i}{n}Z(s)\})\otimes L^{-i}(\lfloor\frac{i}{n}Z(s)\rfloor),

where {in​Z​(s)}\{\frac{i}{n}Z(s)\} is the fractional part of the ℚ{\mathbb{Q}}-divisor in​Z​(s)\frac{i}{n}Z(s), defined componentwise, and for a reduced divisor Σ\Sigma on XX, ΩXp​(log⁡Σ)\Omega^{p}_{X}(\log\Sigma) denotes the sheaf of differential pp-forms ω\omega such that both ω\omega and d​ωd\omega are regular outside Σ\Sigma, and have at most logarithmic poles along the components of Σ\Sigma. If the singularities of Supp⁡Z⁡(s)\operatorname{Supp}Z(s) are at most simple normal crossing, then X¯​[sn]\bar{X}[\sqrt[n]{s}] has at most quotient singularities, and if Y→X¯​[sn]Y\to\bar{X}[\sqrt[n]{s}] is a desingularization, with ν:Y→X\nu\colon Y\to X the induced generically finite morphism, then

ν∗ΩYp=⊕i=0n−1ΩXp(logSupp{inZ(s)})⊗L−i(⌊inZ(s)⌋).\nu_{*}\Omega^{p}_{Y}=\oplus_{i=0}^{n-1}\Omega^{p}_{X}(\log\operatorname{Supp}\{\frac{i}{n}Z(s)\})\otimes L^{-i}(\lfloor\frac{i}{n}Z(s)\rfloor).

This formula is behind the vanishing theorems used in birational classification (see [6, 9, 10]). Statements on divisors of the form KX+∑jbj​Ej+TK_{X}+\sum_{j}b_{j}E_{j}+T, with XX nonsingular, ∑jEj\sum_{j}E_{j} simple normal crossing, bj∈[0,1]b_{j}\in[0,1], and TT a torsion ℚ{\mathbb{Q}}-divisor, are reduced to similar statements on YY with bj∈{0,1}b_{j}\in\{0,1\} and T=0T=0.

Cyclic covers also appear in semistable reduction [8]. In its simplest form, a complex projective family over the unit disc f:𝒳→Δf\colon{\mathcal{X}}\to\Delta has nonsingular general fibers 𝒳t​(t≠0){\mathcal{X}}_{t}\ (t\neq 0), while the special fiber 𝒳0{\mathcal{X}}_{0} is locally cut out by monomials ∏i=1dzimi​(mi∈ℕ)\prod_{i=1}^{d}z_{i}^{m_{i}}\ (m_{i}\in{\mathbb{N}}) with respect to local coordinates z1,…,zdz_{1},\ldots,z_{d}. The family is semistable if moreover 𝒳0{\mathcal{X}}_{0} is reduced. If we base change with tn\sqrt[n]{t} (with nn divisible by all multiplicities mim_{i}), and normalize 𝒳~→𝒳×ΔΔ~\tilde{{\mathcal{X}}}\to{\mathcal{X}}\times_{\Delta}\tilde{\Delta}, the new family 𝒳~→Δ~\tilde{{\mathcal{X}}}\to\tilde{\Delta} has reduced special fiber 𝒳~0\tilde{{\mathcal{X}}}_{0}, and 𝒳~∖𝒳~0⊂𝒳~\tilde{{\mathcal{X}}}\setminus\tilde{{\mathcal{X}}}_{0}\subset\tilde{{\mathcal{X}}} is a quasi-smooth toroidal embedding. If the irreducible components of 𝒳0{\mathcal{X}}_{0} are nonsingular, the toroidal embedding is also strict and 𝒳~\tilde{{\mathcal{X}}} admits a combinatorial desingularization. An equivalent description of 𝒳~\tilde{{\mathcal{X}}} is the normalization of the nn-th root of ff, viewed as a holomorphic function on 𝒳{\mathcal{X}}. Therefore the local computations of [8] give in fact the following statement: if XX is complex manifold, and 0≠s∈Γ⁡(X,Ln)0\neq s\in\Gamma(X,L^{n}) is such that Σ=Supp⁡Z⁡(s)\Sigma=\operatorname{Supp}Z(s) is a normal crossing divisor, then X¯​[sn]∖π¯−1​(Σ)⊂X¯​[sn]\bar{X}[\sqrt[n]{s}]\setminus\bar{\pi}^{-1}(\Sigma)\subset\bar{X}[\sqrt[n]{s}] is a quasi-smooth toroidal embedding, and π¯\bar{\pi} is a toroidal morphism.

Cyclic covers are used to classify the singularities that appear in the birational classification of complex manifolds. Such singularities P∈XP\in X are normal, and the canonical Weil divisor KXK_{X} is a torsion element of Cl⁡(𝒪X,P)\operatorname{Cl}({\mathcal{O}}_{X,P}). If rr is the torsion index, there exists a rational function φ∈ℂ​(X)∗\varphi\in{\mathbb{C}}(X)^{*} such that r​KX=div⁡(φ)rK_{X}=\operatorname{div}(\varphi). The normalization of XX in the Kummer extension ℂ​(X)→ℂ​(X)​(φr){\mathbb{C}}(X)\to{\mathbb{C}}(X)(\sqrt[r]{\varphi}) becomes a cyclic cover P′∈X′→πP∈XP^{\prime}\in X^{\prime}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\pi}}{{\to}}P\in X. It is called the index one cover of P∈XP\in X, since being étale in codimension one, KX′=π∗​KX∼0K_{X^{\prime}}=\pi^{*}K_{X}\sim 0. The known method to classify P∈XP\in X is to first classify the index one cover, and then understand all possible actions of cyclic groups (see [14]).

We have discussed so far roots of rational functions, (normalized) roots of multi sections of line bundles, and index one covers of torsion ℚ{\mathbb{Q}}-divisors on normal varieties. This paper gives a unified treatment of all these concepts, based on normalized roots of rational functions on normal varieties. Moreover, we show that the cyclic covering trick can be performed inside the category of quasi-smooth toroidal embeddings. In order to prove vanishing theorems, we no longer have to assume that the base is nonsingular, or to resolve the singularities of the total space of the covering.

To state the main results of this paper, let kk be an algebraically closed field.

Theorem 0.1.

Let X/kX/k be an normal algebraic variety. Let φ\varphi be an invertible rational function on XX, let nn be a positive integer such that char⁡k∤n\operatorname{char}k\nmid n. Denote D=1n​div⁡(φ)D=\frac{1}{n}\operatorname{div}(\varphi), so that DD is a ℚ{\mathbb{Q}}-Weil divisor on XX with n​D∼0nD\sim 0. Let π:Y→X\pi\colon Y\to X be the normalization of XX with respect to the ring extension

k⁡(X)→k​(X)​[T](Tn−φ).k(X)\to\frac{k(X)[T]}{(T^{n}-\varphi)}.

The right hand side is a product of fields (the function fields of the irreducible components of YY), and YY identifies with the disjoint union of the normalization of XX in each field. By construction, Y/kY/k is a normal algebraic variety (possibly disconnected).

  • a)

    The class of TT becomes an invertible rational function ψ\psi on YY such that ψn=π∗​φ\psi^{n}=\pi^{*}\varphi. We have π∗​D=div⁡(ψ)\pi^{*}D=\operatorname{div}(\psi) and

    π∗𝒪Y=⊕i=0n−1𝒪X(⌊iD⌋)⋅ψi.\pi_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{Y}=\oplus_{i=0}^{n-1}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}(\lfloor iD\rfloor)\cdot\psi^{i}.

    The morphism π\pi is étale exactly over X∖Supp⁡{D}X\setminus\operatorname{Supp}\{D\}, where {D}\{D\} is the fractional part of the ℚ{\mathbb{Q}}-divisor DD, defined componentwise. It is flat if and only if the Weil divisors ⌊i​D⌋​(0<i<n)\lfloor iD\rfloor\ (0<i<n) are Cartier.

  • b)

    Suppose U⊆XU\subseteq X is a quasi-smooth toroidal embedding and D|UD|_{U} has integer coefficients. Then π−1​(U)⊆Y\pi^{-1}(U)\subseteq Y is a quasi-smooth toroidal embedding, and π\pi is a toroidal morphism. Denote ΣX=X∖U\Sigma_{X}=X\setminus U and ΣY=Y∖π−1​(U)\Sigma_{Y}=Y\setminus\pi^{-1}(U). Then π∗​Ω~X/kp​(log⁡ΣX)​→∼​Ω~Y/kp​(log⁡ΣY)\pi^{*}\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma_{X}){\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}}\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{Y/k}(\log\Sigma_{Y}), and by the projection formula

    π∗​Ω~Y/kp​(log⁡ΣY)=Ω~X/kp​(log⁡ΣX)⊗π∗​𝒪Y.\pi_{*}\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{Y/k}(\log\Sigma_{Y})=\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma_{X})\otimes\pi_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{Y}.
Theorem 0.2.

Suppose char⁡k=0\operatorname{char}k=0. Let U⊆XU\subseteq X and U′⊆X′U^{\prime}\subseteq X^{\prime} be toroidal embeddings over kk, let μ:X′→X\mu\colon X^{\prime}\to X be a proper morphism which induces an isomorphism U′​→∼​UU^{\prime}{\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}}U. Denote ΣX=X∖U\Sigma_{X}=X\setminus U and ΣX′=X′∖ΣX′\Sigma_{X^{\prime}}=X^{\prime}\setminus\Sigma_{X^{\prime}}. Then

Rq​μ∗​Ω~X′/kp​(log⁡ΣX′)={Ω~X/kp​(log⁡ΣX)q=00q≠0R^{q}\mu_{*}\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X^{\prime}/k}(\log\Sigma_{X^{\prime}})=\left\{\begin{array}[]{lll}\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma_{X})&q=0\\ 0&q\neq 0\end{array}\right.

Theorem 0.1 generalizes the known cyclic covering trick (see [6, Section 3], especially 3.3-3.11), where the base space XX is assumed nonsingular, to the case when XX is just normal. Statement a) is elementary. The toroidal part of b) is implicit in [8] if (X,ΣX)(X,\Sigma_{X}) is log smooth, as already mentioned. The general case (Theorem 3.8) is proved by reduction to the following fact: the normalized root of a toric variety with respect to a torus character consists of several isomorphic copies of a toric morphism (Proposition 3.7). The sheaf Ω~X/kp​(log⁡ΣX)\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma_{X}) consists of the rational pp-forms ω\omega of XX such that both ω,d​ω\omega,d\omega are regular near the prime divisors of XX outside ΣX\Sigma_{X}, and have at most simple poles at the prime components of ΣX\Sigma_{X}. It is called the sheaf of logarithmic pp-forms of (X/k,ΣX)(X/k,\Sigma_{X}), in the sense of Zariski-Steenbrink. It is constructed by ignoring closed subsets of XX of codimension at least two, so in general it is singular. But if X∖ΣX⊂XX\setminus\Sigma_{X}\subset X is a toroidal embedding, it is locally free [15, 3]. If XX is nonsingular and ΣX\Sigma_{X} is a normal crossing divisor, this sheaf coincides with the sheaf of logarithmic forms ΩX/kp​(log⁡ΣX)\Omega^{p}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma_{X}) in the sense of Deligne (see [6] for the algebraic version, with ΣX\Sigma_{X} assumed simple normal crossing). If ΣX=0\Sigma_{X}=0, then Ω~X/kp=Ω~X/kp​(log⁡0)\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}=\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(\log 0) is the double dual of the usual sheaf of Kähler differentials ΩX/kp\Omega^{p}_{X/k}. We note that differential forms or vector fields on YY can be computed without the toroidal assumption (Lemma 3.6).

Theorem 0.2 is the invariance of the logarithmic sheaves under different toroidal embeddings, proved by Esnault and Viehweg [5, Lemma 1.5] in the case when XX is projective nonsingular and ΣX\Sigma_{X} has normal crossings. One corollary is that

Hq​(X,Ω~X/kp​(log⁡ΣX))→Hq​(X′,Ω~X′/kp​(log⁡ΣX′))H^{q}(X,\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma_{X}))\to H^{q}(X^{\prime},\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X^{\prime}/k}(\log\Sigma_{X^{\prime}}))

is an isomorphism for every p,qp,q. If XX is proper and (X,X∖U)(X,X\setminus U) is log smooth, the corollary follows from the E1E_{1}-degeneration of the spectral sequence induced in hypercohomology by the logarithmic De Rham complex endowed with the naive filtration (Deligne [4]). If XX is projective and X∖UX\setminus U is a simple normal crossing divisor, Esnault-Viehweg [5, Lemma 1.5] proved that the corollary implies Theorem 0.2. We use the same idea, combined with a result of Bierstone-Milman [2], in order to compactify strict log smooth toroidal embeddings (Corollary 1.11).

The normalization of roots of multi sections of line bundles on normal varieties, and the index one covers torsion ℚ{\mathbb{Q}}-divisors on normal varieties, are both examples of normalized roots of rational functions. In practice, index one covers are most useful. They preserve irreducibility, so one can work in the classical setting of function fields. Their drawback is that they do not commute with base change to open subsets. For this reason, at least for proofs, we need to consider normalized roots of rational functions, which commute with étale base change.

1. Preliminaries

We consider varieties (reduced, possibly reducible), defined over an algebraically closed field kk.

1-A. Zariski-Steenbrink differentials [16, 15]

Let X/kX/k be a normal variety. Its connected components coincide with its irreducible components. Let k⁡(X)k(X) be the ring of rational functions of XX, consisting of functions regular on a dense open subset of XX. It identifies with the product of the function fields of the irreducible components of XX. A rational function is invertible if and only if it is not zero on each irreducible component.

Let ω∈Ωk⁡(X)/kp\omega\in\Omega^{p}_{k(X)/k} be a rational differential pp-form. Let E⊂XE\subset X be a prime divisor. The form ω\omega is regular at EE if it can be written as a sum of forms f0⋅d​f1∧⋯∧d​fpf_{0}\cdot df_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge df_{p}, with fi∈𝒪X,Ef_{i}\in{\mathcal{O}}_{X,E}. The form ω\omega has at most a logarithmic pole at EE if both ω\omega and d​ωd\omega have at most a simple pole at EE. If tt is a local parameter at the generic point of EE, this is equivalent to the existence of a decomposition ω=d​tt∧ωp−1+ωp,\omega=\frac{dt}{t}\wedge\omega^{p-1}+\omega^{p}, with ωp−1,ωp\omega^{p-1},\omega^{p} rational differentials regular at EE. If E¯→E\bar{E}\to E is the normalization, the restriction ωp−1|E¯\omega^{p-1}|_{\bar{E}} is independent of the decomposition, called the residue of ω\omega at EE. The residue is zero if and only if ω\omega is regular at EE.

For an open subset U⊆XU\subseteq X, let Γ⁡(U,Ω~X/kp)\Gamma(U,\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}) consist of the rational differential pp-forms which are regular at each prime divisor of XX which intersects UU. This defines a coherent 𝒪X{\mathcal{O}}_{X}-module Ω~X/kp\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}, called the sheaf of pp-differential forms of X/kX/k, in the sense of Zariski-Steenbrink. If j:X0⊂Xj\colon X^{0}\subset X is the nonsingular locus of XX, Ω~X/kp=j∗​(ΩX0/kp)\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}=j_{*}(\Omega^{p}_{X^{0}/k}). If DD is a Weil divisor on XX, let Γ⁡(U,Ω~X/kp​(D))\Gamma(U,\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(D)) consist of the rational differential pp-forms ω\omega such that tEmultE⁡D​ωt_{E}^{\operatorname{mult}_{E}D}\omega is regular at EE, for every prime divisor EE, with local parameter tEt_{E}. This defines a coherent 𝒪X{\mathcal{O}}_{X}-module Ω~X/kp​(D)\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(D). We have Ω~X/kp​(D)=j∗​(ΩX0/kp⊗𝒪X0​(D|X0))\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(D)=j_{*}(\Omega^{p}_{X^{0}/k}\otimes{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{0}}(D|_{X^{0}})).

Let Σ\Sigma be a reduced Weil divisor on XX, or equivalently, a finite set of prime divisors on XX. For an open subset U⊆XU\subseteq X, let Γ⁡(U,Ω~X/kp​(log⁡Σ))\Gamma(U,\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma)) consist of the rational differential pp-forms ω\omega such that for every prime divisor EE which intersects UU, ω\omega is regular (has at most a logarithmic pole) at EE if E∉ΣE\notin\Sigma (E∈ΣE\in\Sigma). This defines a coherent 𝒪X{\mathcal{O}}_{X}-module Ω~X/kp​(log⁡Σ)\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma), called the sheaf of logarithmic pp-differential forms of (X/k,Σ)(X/k,\Sigma), in the sense of Zariski-Steenbrink. For a Weil divisor DD on XX, we can similarly define Ω~X/kp​(log⁡Σ)​(D)\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma)(D).

The tangent sheaf 𝒯X/k{\mathcal{T}}_{X/k} is already S2S_{2}-saturated, since XX is normal: a derivation θ\theta of k⁡(X)/kk(X)/k is regular on an open subset U⊆XU\subseteq X if and only if it is regular at each prime of XX which intersects UU. For an open subset U⊆XU\subseteq X, let Γ⁡(U,𝒯~X/k​(−log⁡Σ))\Gamma(U,\tilde{{\mathcal{T}}}_{X/k}(-\log\Sigma)) consist of the derivations θ∈Γ⁡(U,𝒯X/k)\theta\in\Gamma(U,{\mathcal{T}}_{X/k}) such that for every prime divisor E∈ΣE\in\Sigma which intersects UU, θ\theta preserves the maximal ideal 𝔪X,E{\mathfrak{m}}_{X,E}. This defines a coherent 𝒪X{\mathcal{O}}_{X}-module 𝒯~X/k​(−log⁡Σ)\tilde{{\mathcal{T}}}_{X/k}(-\log\Sigma), called the sheaf of logarithmic derivations of (X,Σ)(X,\Sigma), in the sense of Zariski-Steenbrink. For a Weil divisor DD on XX, we can similarly define 𝒯~X/k​(D),𝒯~X/k​(−log⁡Σ)​(D)\tilde{{\mathcal{T}}}_{X/k}(D),\tilde{{\mathcal{T}}}_{X/k}(-\log\Sigma)(D).

Lemma 1.1.

Let u:X′→Xu\colon X^{\prime}\to X be an étale morphism. In particular, X′X^{\prime} is normal. Let Σ\Sigma be a reduced Weil divisor on XX, denote Σ′=u−1​(Σ)\Sigma^{\prime}=u^{-1}(\Sigma). Then we have base change isomorphisms

u∗​Ω~X/kp​→∼​Ω~X′/kp​ and ​u∗​Ω~X/kp​(log⁡Σ)​→∼​Ω~X′/kp​(log⁡Σ′).u^{*}\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}{\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}}\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X^{\prime}/k}\text{ and }u^{*}\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma){\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}}\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X^{\prime}/k}(\log\Sigma^{\prime}).

Since uu is flat, the base change homomorphism u∗​iV∗​ΩV/kp​(log⁡Σ|V)→iV′∗​v∗​ΩV/kp​(log⁡Σ|V)u^{*}{i_{V}}_{*}\Omega^{p}_{V/k}(\log\Sigma|_{V})\to{{i_{V^{\prime}}}_{*}}v^{*}\Omega^{p}_{V/k}(\log\Sigma|_{V}) is an isomorphism. Since vv is smooth, v∗​ΩV/kp​(log⁡Σ|V)→ΩV′/kp​(log⁡Σ′|V′)v^{*}\Omega^{p}_{V/k}(\log\Sigma|_{V})\to\Omega^{p}_{V^{\prime}/k}(\log\Sigma^{\prime}|_{V^{\prime}}) is an isomorphism. Therefore the base change isomorphism becomes u∗​Ω~X/kp​(log⁡Σ)​→∼​Ω~X′/kp​(log⁡Σ′)u^{*}\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma){\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}}\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X^{\prime}/k}(\log\Sigma^{\prime}). ∎

Lemma 1.2.

Let u:X′→Xu\colon X^{\prime}\to X be an étale morphism. Let E′E^{\prime} be a prime divisor on X′X^{\prime}, let EE be the closure of u⁡(E′)u(E^{\prime}). Let ω\omega be a rational pp-form on XX. Then

  • i)

    ω\omega is regular at EE if and only if u∗​ωu^{*}\omega is regular at E′E^{\prime}.

  • ii)

    ω\omega has at most a log pole at EE if and only if u∗​ωu^{*}\omega has at most a log pole at E′E^{\prime}.

Proof.

i) There exists l≫0l\gg 0 such that ω∈Ω~Xp​(l​E)E\omega\in\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X}(lE)_{E}. By Lemma 1.1, the inclusion Ω~X/kp⊂Ω~X/kp​(l​E)\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}\subset\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(lE) becomes after étale pullback Ω~X′/kp⊂Ω~X′/kp​(l​E′)\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X^{\prime}/k}\subset\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X^{\prime}/k}(lE^{\prime}). All sheaves that appear being coherent, the section ω∈Ω~X/kp​(l​E)E\omega\in\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(lE)_{E} belongs to (Ω~X/kp)E(\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k})_{E} if and only the pullback section u∗​ω∈Ω~X′/kp​(l​E′)E′u^{*}\omega\in\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X^{\prime}/k}(lE^{\prime})_{E^{\prime}} belongs to (Ω~X′/kp)E′(\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X^{\prime}/k})_{E^{\prime}}

ii) The proof in the logarithmic case is similar. ∎

Lemma 1.3.

Let u:X′→Xu\colon X^{\prime}\to X be an étale morphism. Let DD be a ℚ{\mathbb{Q}}-Weil divisor on XX. Let D′=u∗​DD^{\prime}=u^{*}D be the pullback ℚ{\mathbb{Q}}-Weil divisor, defined by restricting to big open subsets. Then

u∗​𝒪X​(⌊D⌋)​→∼​𝒪X′​(⌊D′⌋).u^{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}(\lfloor D\rfloor){\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}}{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}(\lfloor D^{\prime}\rfloor).
Proof.

Restrict to the smooth loci of X′X^{\prime} and XX. Round down commutes with pullback since uu is unramified in codimension one. By flat base change, the isomorphism extends to X′X^{\prime} and XX. ∎

1-B. Zariski-Steenbrink differentials and derivations on toric varieties [3, 12]

Let MM be a lattice, with dual lattice N=M∗N=M^{*}. Let T=TN=Hom⁡(M,k∗)T=T_{N}=\operatorname{Hom}(M,k^{*}) be the induced torus over kk. The torus acts on the space of global regular functions, with eigenspace decomposition

Γ(T,𝒪T)=⊕m∈Mk⋅χm.\Gamma(T,{\mathcal{O}}_{T})=\oplus_{m\in M}k\cdot\chi^{m}.

Recall that each element m∈Mm\in M induces by evaluation a torus character χm:T→k∗\chi^{m}\colon T\to k^{*}. Denote αm=d⁡(χm)χm∈Γ⁡(T,ΩT/k)\alpha_{m}=\frac{d(\chi^{m})}{\chi^{m}}\in\Gamma(T,\Omega_{T/k}). The application m↦αmm\mapsto\alpha_{m} is additive, and induces an isomorphism

𝒪T⊗ℤM​→∼​ΩT/k, 1⊗m↦αm.{\mathcal{O}}_{T}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}M{\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}}\Omega_{T/k},\ 1\otimes m\mapsto\alpha_{m}.

This follows from computations on the affine space, since a choice of basis m1,…,mnm_{1},\ldots,m_{n} of MM, with induced characters zi=χmiz_{i}=\chi^{m_{i}}, identifies TT with the principal open set D⁡(∏i=1nzi)⊂𝔸knD(\prod_{i=1}^{n}z_{i})\subset{\mathbb{A}}^{n}_{k}. In particular, we obtain isomorphisms

𝒪T⊗ℤ∧pM→∼ΩpT/k, 1⊗m↦αm.{\mathcal{O}}_{T}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\wedge^{p}M{\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}}\Omega^{p}_{T/k},\ 1\otimes m\mapsto\alpha_{m}.

Passing to global sections, the image of k⊗ℤMk\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}M is V⊂Γ⁡(T,ΩT/k)V\subset\Gamma(T,\Omega_{T/k}), the subspace of global 11-forms invariant under the torus action. We have induced eigenspace decompositions

Γ(T,ΩT/kp)=⊕m∈Mχm⋅∧pV.\Gamma(T,\Omega^{p}_{T/k})=\oplus_{m\in M}\chi^{m}\cdot\wedge^{p}V.

So every regular form ω∈Γ⁡(T,ΩT/kp)\omega\in\Gamma(T,\Omega^{p}_{T/k}) admits a unique decomposition

ω=∑m∈Mχm⋅ω(m)(ω(m)∈∧pV).\omega=\sum_{m\in M}\chi^{m}\cdot\omega(m)\ (\omega(m)\in\wedge^{p}V).

For e∈Ne\in N, there exists a unique kk-derivation θe\theta_{e} of Γ⁡(T,𝒪T)\Gamma(T,{\mathcal{O}}_{T}) such that θe​(χm)=⟨m,e⟩​χm\theta_{e}(\chi^{m})=\langle m,e\rangle\chi^{m} for every m∈Mm\in M. The application α:N→Γ⁡(T,𝒯T/k),e↦θe\alpha\colon N\to\Gamma(T,{\mathcal{T}}_{T/k}),e\mapsto\theta_{e} is additive and induces an isomorphism of 𝒪T{\mathcal{O}}_{T}-modules

1⊗ℤα:𝒪T⊗ℤN→𝒯T/k.1\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\alpha\colon{\mathcal{O}}_{T}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}N\to{\mathcal{T}}_{T/k}.

Passing to global sections, the image of k⊗ℤNk\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}N is W⊂Γ⁡(T,𝒯T/k)W\subset\Gamma(T,{\mathcal{T}}_{T/k}), the space of derivations invariant under the torus action. We have an eigenspace decomposition

Γ(T,𝒯T/k)=⊕m∈MχmW.\Gamma(T,{\mathcal{T}}_{T/k})=\oplus_{m\in M}\chi^{m}W.

θ=∑m∈Mχm​θ​(m)​(θ⁡(m)∈W).\theta=\sum_{m\in M}\chi^{m}\theta(m)\ (\theta(m)\in W).

As in [3, Lemma 4.3.1] or  [12, Proposition 3.1], we obtain the following explict formulas:

Let e∈Ne\in N be a primitive vector. Theorem 1.5.

1-C. Toroidal embeddings [8]

A toroidal embedding is an open subset U⊆XU\subseteq X in a normal variety X/kX/k, such that for every P∈XP\in X, there exists an affine toric variety Z=TN​emb⁡(σ)Z=T_{N}\operatorname{emb}(\sigma), a point Q∈ZQ\in Z, and an isomorphism of complete local kk-algebras

𝒪^X,P≃𝒪^Z,Q\hat{{\mathcal{O}}}_{X,P}\simeq\hat{{\mathcal{O}}}_{Z,Q}

such that X∖UX\setminus U corresponds to Z∖TNZ\setminus T_{N}. It follows that UU is nonsingular, and Σ=X∖U\Sigma=X\setminus U has pure codimension one. If each irreducible component of Σ\Sigma is normal, the toroidal embedding is called strict. A toroidal morphism f:(U′⊆X′)→(U⊆X)f\colon(U^{\prime}\subseteq X^{\prime})\to(U\subseteq X) of toroidal embeddings is a morphism f:X′→Xf\colon X^{\prime}\to X, such that for every P′∈X′P^{\prime}\in X^{\prime}, we can choose local formal isomorphisms as above such that 𝒪^X,f⁡(P′)→𝒪^X′,P′\hat{{\mathcal{O}}}_{X,f(P^{\prime})}\to\hat{{\mathcal{O}}}_{X^{\prime},P^{\prime}} corresponds to the morphism 𝒪^Z,g⁡(Q′)→𝒪^Z′,Q′\hat{{\mathcal{O}}}_{Z,g(Q^{\prime})}\to\hat{{\mathcal{O}}}_{Z^{\prime},Q^{\prime}} induced by a toric morphism g:Z→Z′g\colon Z\to Z^{\prime}. It follows that f⁡(U′)⊆Uf(U^{\prime})\subseteq U.

Given a local formal isomorphism as above, there exists by [1, Corollary 2.6] a hut

with u,vu,v étale, u⁡(P′)=Pu(P^{\prime})=P, v⁡(P′)=Qv(P^{\prime})=Q, and u−1​(U)=U′=v−1​(TN)u^{-1}(U)=U^{\prime}=v^{-1}(T_{N}). By Theorem 1.5 and Lemma 1.1, we obtain

Theorem 1.6.

Let U⊆X/kU\subseteq X/k be a toroidal embedding. Then Ω~X/k1​(log⁡Σ)\tilde{\Omega}^{1}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma) is a locally trivial 𝒪X{\mathcal{O}}_{X}-module of rank equal to the dimension of XX, and ∧pΩ~X/k1(logΣ)→∼Ω~X/kp(logΣ)\wedge^{p}\tilde{\Omega}^{1}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma){\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}}\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma).

Proposition 1.7.

Let U⊆XU\subseteq X and V⊆YV\subseteq Y be toroidal embeddings. Let f:X→Yf\colon X\to Y be a morphism such that f⁡(U)⊆Vf(U)\subseteq V. The pullback homomorphism ΩV/k∙→f∗​ΩU/k∙\Omega_{V/k}^{\bullet}\to f_{*}\Omega^{\bullet}_{U/k} extends (uniquely) to a homomorphism

Ω~Y/k∙​(log⁡ΣY)→f∗​Ω~X/k∙​(log⁡ΣX).\tilde{\Omega}_{Y/k}^{\bullet}(\log\Sigma_{Y})\to f_{*}\tilde{\Omega}^{\bullet}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma_{X}).

We prove the claim in two steps.

Then Ω~Z/k1​(log⁡ΣZ)\tilde{\Omega}^{1}_{Z/k}(\log\Sigma_{Z}) is the free 𝒪Z{\mathcal{O}}_{Z}-module with basis d​titi​(1≤i≤n),\frac{dt_{i}}{t_{i}}\ (1\leq i\leq n), and ∧pΩZ/k1(logΣZ)→∼ΩY/kp(logΣY)\wedge^{p}\Omega^{1}_{Z/k}(\log\Sigma_{Z}){\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}}\Omega^{p}_{Y/k}(\log\Sigma_{Y}). By Lemma 1.1, v∗​Ω~Z/k∙​(log⁡ΣZ)​→∼​Ω~Y/k∙​(log⁡ΣY)v^{*}\tilde{\Omega}_{Z/k}^{\bullet}(\log\Sigma_{Z}){\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}}\tilde{\Omega}_{Y/k}^{\bullet}(\log\Sigma_{Y}). Denote zi=v∗​ti​(1≤i≤n)z_{i}=v^{*}t_{i}\ (1\leq i\leq n). Then zi∈Γ⁡(V,𝒪V∗)z_{i}\in\Gamma(V,{\mathcal{O}}_{V}^{*}), Ω~Y/k1​(log⁡ΣY)\tilde{\Omega}^{1}_{Y/k}(\log\Sigma_{Y}) is the free 𝒪Y{\mathcal{O}}_{Y}-module with basis

ωi=d​zizi∈Γ⁡(Y,Ω~Y/k1​(log⁡ΣY))​(1≤i≤n),\omega_{i}=\frac{dz_{i}}{z_{i}}\in\Gamma(Y,\tilde{\Omega}^{1}_{Y/k}(\log\Sigma_{Y}))\ (1\leq i\leq n),

and ∧pΩ~Y/k1(logΣY)→∼Ω~Y/kp(logΣY)\wedge^{p}\tilde{\Omega}^{1}_{Y/k}(\log\Sigma_{Y}){\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}}\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{Y/k}(\log\Sigma_{Y}). Therefore, in order to prove the claim, it suffices to show that f∗​ωi∈Γ⁡(X,Ω~X/k1​(log⁡ΣX))f^{*}\omega_{i}\in\Gamma(X,\tilde{\Omega}^{1}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma_{X})). But gi=f∗​zi∈Γ⁡(U,𝒪U∗)g_{i}=f^{*}z_{i}\in\Gamma(U,{\mathcal{O}}_{U}^{*}), and

The claim holds in this case.

Step 2: The claim is local on YY, so we may shrink YY to an affine open neighborhood of a fixed point. By [1], there exists a hut

where T⊆ZT\subseteq Z is a torus embedding, u,vu,v are étale, and u−1​(V)=V′=v−1​(T)u^{-1}(V)=V^{\prime}=v^{-1}(T). Denote X′=X×YY′X^{\prime}=X\times_{Y}Y^{\prime}, and consider the base change diagram

Denote U′=u′−1​(U)U^{\prime}={u^{\prime}}^{-1}(U). The restriction of the cartesian diagram to open subsets is also cartesian

Since u′u^{\prime} is étale, U′⊆X′U^{\prime}\subseteq X^{\prime} is also a toroidal embedding. Let ω∈Γ⁡(Y,ΩY/kp​(log⁡ΣY))\omega\in\Gamma(Y,\Omega^{p}_{Y/k}(\log\Sigma_{Y})). Then ω|V∈Γ⁡(V,ΩV/kp)\omega|_{V}\in\Gamma(V,\Omega^{p}_{V/k}), so η=f∗​(ω|V)∈Γ⁡(U,ΩU/kp)\eta=f^{*}(\omega|_{V})\in\Gamma(U,\Omega^{p}_{U/k}). We have u′∗​η=f′∗​u∗​ω{u^{\prime}}^{*}\eta={f^{\prime}}^{*}u^{*}\omega. By Lemma 1.1, u∗​ω∈Γ⁡(Y′,Ω~Y′/kp​(log⁡ΣY′))u^{*}\omega\in\Gamma(Y^{\prime},\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{Y^{\prime}/k}(\log\Sigma_{Y^{\prime}})). By Step 1, f′∗​u∗​ω∈Γ⁡(X′,Ω~X′/kp​(log⁡ΣX′)){f^{\prime}}^{*}u^{*}\omega\in\Gamma(X^{\prime},\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X^{\prime}/k}(\log\Sigma_{X^{\prime}})). Therefore u′∗​η{u^{\prime}}^{*}\eta has at most logarithmic poles along the primes of ΣX′\Sigma_{X^{\prime}}. By Lemma 1.2, η∈Γ⁡(X,Ω~X/kp​(log⁡ΣX))\eta\in\Gamma(X,\tilde{\Omega}^{p}_{X/k}(\log\Sigma_{X})). ∎

1-D. Log smooth embeddings

A log smooth embedding is a toroidal embedding U⊆XU\subseteq X such that X/kX/k is smooth. If we denote Σ=X∖U\Sigma=X\setminus U, this is equivalent to (X,Σ)(X,\Sigma) being a log smooth pair, that is X/kX/k is smooth and the restriction of Σ\Sigma to each connected component of XX is either empty, or a normal crossing divisor. A log smooth embedding is called strict if it is so as a toroidal embedding. This is equivalent to the property that each irreducible component of Σ\Sigma is smooth, that is Σ\Sigma is a simple normal crossing divisor. We obtain an equivalence between (strict) log smooth embeddings and (strict) log smooth pairs.

We assume char⁡k=0\operatorname{char}k=0. We need the special case E=0E=0 of [2, Theorem 3.4]:

Theorem 1.8 (Bierstone-Milman).

Let XX be a smooth irreducible variety, let Σ\Sigma be a reduced divisor on XX. Let VV be an open subset of XX such that Σ|V\Sigma|_{V} has at most simple normal crossing singularities. Then there exists a proper morphism σ:X′→X\sigma\colon X^{\prime}\to X such that

  • a)

    X′X^{\prime} is smooth and σ−1​Σ\sigma^{-1}\Sigma has at most simple normal crossing singularities.

  • b)

    σ:σ−1​(V)→V\sigma\colon\sigma^{-1}(V)\to V is an isomorphism.

Lemma 1.9.

Let U⊆XU\subseteq X be an open dense embedding, with UU smooth. Then there exists a proper morphism σ:X′→X\sigma\colon X^{\prime}\to X such that σ:σ−1​(U)→U\sigma\colon\sigma^{-1}(U)\to U is an isomorphism and σ−1​(U)⊆X′\sigma^{-1}(U)\subseteq X^{\prime} is a strict log smooth open embedding.

Proof.

Since UU is smooth, the singular locus of XX is contained in X∖UX\setminus U. By Hironaka’s strong resolution of singularities, there exists a proper morphism σ:X′→X\sigma\colon X^{\prime}\to X such that X′X^{\prime} is smooth, σ−1​(U)→U\sigma^{-1}(U)\to U is an isomorphism, and the complement of σ−1​(U)\sigma^{-1}(U) in XX is a SNC divisor. The open embedding σ−1​(U)⊆X′\sigma^{-1}(U)\subseteq X^{\prime} is therefore strict log smooth, and satisfies the desired properties. ∎

Lemma 1.10.

Let U⊆XU\subseteq X and X⊆YX\subseteq Y be open dense embeddings.

  • 1)

    If U⊆YU\subseteq Y is a strict log smooth embedding, so is U⊆XU\subseteq X.

  • 2)

    Suppose U⊆XU\subseteq X is a strict log smooth embedding. Then there exists a proper morphism σ:Y′→Y\sigma\colon Y^{\prime}\to Y such that σ:σ−1​(X)→X\sigma\colon\sigma^{-1}(X)\to X is an isomorphism and the open embedding σ−1​(U)⊆Y′\sigma^{-1}(U)\subseteq Y^{\prime} is strict log smooth.

Proof.

1) Since YY is smooth, so is XX. The divisor Y∖UY\setminus U is SNC on YY, hence so is its restriction (Y∖U)|X=X∖U(Y\setminus U)|_{X}=X\setminus U. Therefore U⊆XU\subseteq X is strict log smooth.

2) Since U⊆XU\subseteq X is strict log smooth, XX is smooth. By Lemma 1.9 for X⊆YX\subseteq Y, we may replace YY by a modification outside XX, so that X⊆YX\subseteq Y is also strict log smooth. Let Σ=Y∖U=(Y∖X)∪(X∖U)\Sigma=Y\setminus U=(Y\setminus X)\cup(X\setminus U). Then Σ\Sigma is a divisor on YY. Its restriction to XX is Σ|X=X∖U\Sigma|_{X}=X\setminus U, a SNC divisor by assumption. By Theorem 1.8, we may replace YY by a modification outside XX so that Σ\Sigma becomes a SNC divisor on YY. Therefore U⊆YU\subseteq Y is strict log smooth. ∎

Corollary 1.11.

Let U⊆XU\subseteq X be a strict log smooth embedding. Then there exists an open embedding j:X⊆X¯j\colon X\subseteq\bar{X} such that the induced open embedding U⊆X¯U\subseteq\bar{X} is strict log smooth, and X¯/k\bar{X}/k is proper.

Proof.

By Nagata, there exists an open dense embedding X⊆X¯X\subseteq\bar{X}, with X¯/k\bar{X}/k proper. By Lemma 1.10.2), we may replace X¯\bar{X} by a modification outside XX, so that the induced embedding U⊆X¯U\subseteq\bar{X} is strict log smooth. ∎

Corollary 1.12.

Let U⊆XU\subseteq X and V⊆YV\subseteq Y be strict log smooth open embeddings. Let f:X→Yf\colon X\to Y be a morphism such that f⁡(U)⊆Vf(U)\subseteq V. Then there exists a commutative diagram

such that

  • a)

    the vertical arrows are open embeddings.

  • b)

    U⊆X¯U\subseteq\bar{X} and V⊆Y¯V\subseteq\bar{Y} are strict log smooth embeddings.

  • c)

    X¯\bar{X} and Y¯\bar{Y} are proper over kk.

Moreover, ff is proper if and only if X=f¯−1​(Y)X={\bar{f}}^{-1}(Y).

Proof.

By Corollary 1.11, there exists an open embedding Y⊆Y¯Y\subseteq\bar{Y} such that Y¯\bar{Y} is proper and V⊆Y¯V\subseteq\bar{Y} is strict log smooth. By Nagata, there exists an open embedding X⊆X′X\subseteq X^{\prime} with X′X^{\prime} proper. Then ff induces a rational map f¯:X′⇢Y¯\bar{f}\colon X^{\prime}\dashrightarrow\bar{Y}. Let Γ\Gamma be the graph of f¯\bar{f}, with induced morphisms to X′X^{\prime} and Y¯\bar{Y}, which partially resolve f¯\bar{f}. Since f¯\bar{f} is defined over XX, Γ→X′\Gamma\to X^{\prime} is an isomorphism over XX. We obtain a chain of open embeddings U⊆X⊆ΓU\subseteq X\subseteq\Gamma. By Lemma 1.10.2), we may replace Γ\Gamma by a modification outside XX, denoted X¯\bar{X}, such that U⊆X¯U\subseteq\bar{X} is strict log smooth. This ends the construction of the diagram. The long exact sequences for hypercohomology with supports induce a commutative diagram with exact rows

Theorem 1.17.

Let (X′,Σ′),(X,Σ)(X^{\prime},\Sigma^{\prime}),(X,\Sigma) be strict log smooth pairs, let f:X′→Xf\colon X^{\prime}\to X be a proper morphism such that f:X′∖Σ′→X∖Σf\colon X^{\prime}\setminus\Sigma^{\prime}\to X\setminus\Sigma is an isomorphism. Then for every pp, the natural homomorphism

Denote α:ΩXp​(log⁡Σ)→R​f∗​ΩX′p​(log⁡Σ′)\alpha\colon\Omega^{p}_{X}(\log\Sigma)\to Rf_{*}\Omega^{p}_{X^{\prime}}(\log\Sigma^{\prime}). We prove by induction on dimX\dim X that α\alpha is a quasi-isomorphism. If dimX=1\dim X=1, then ff is an isomorphism and the claim is clear. Suppose dimX≥2\dim X\geq 2. Let ZZ be the complement of the largest open subset of XX where α\alpha is a quasi-isomorphism. It is the union of the supports of the following 𝒪X{\mathcal{O}}_{X}-modules: the cokernel 𝒞{\mathcal{C}} of ΩXp​(log⁡Σ)→f∗​ΩX′p​(log⁡Σ′)\Omega^{p}_{X}(\log\Sigma)\to f_{*}\Omega^{p}_{X^{\prime}}(\log\Sigma^{\prime}), and Ri​f∗​ΩX′p​(log⁡Σ′)​(i>0)R^{i}f_{*}\Omega^{p}_{X^{\prime}}(\log\Sigma^{\prime})\ (i>0). Suppose by contradiction that ZZ is nonempty.

Step 1: We claim that dimZ≤0\dim Z\leq 0. Indeed, the statement is local on XX, so we may suppose XX is affine. Let HH be a general hyperplane section of XX. Denote H′=f∗​HH^{\prime}=f^{*}H. Then (H,Σ|H)(H,\Sigma|_{H}) and (H′,Σ′|H′)(H^{\prime},\Sigma^{\prime}|_{H^{\prime}}) are strict log smooth, and g=f|H′:H′→Hg=f|_{H^{\prime}}\colon H^{\prime}\to H maps H∖(Σ|H)H\setminus(\Sigma|_{H}) isomorphically onto H′∖(Σ′|H′)H^{\prime}\setminus(\Sigma^{\prime}|_{H^{\prime}}). By induction, ΩHp​(log⁡Σ|H)→R​g∗​ΩH′p​(log⁡Σ′|H′)\Omega^{p}_{H}(\log\Sigma|_{H})\to Rg_{*}\Omega^{p}_{H^{\prime}}(\log\Sigma^{\prime}|_{H^{\prime}}) is a quasi-isomorphism.

Since HH is general, we have base change isomorphisms

For i>0i>0, the right hand side is zero, and therefore Ri​f∗​ΩX′p​(log⁡Σ′)|HR^{i}f_{*}\Omega^{p}_{X^{\prime}}(\log\Sigma^{\prime})|_{H} is zero. For i=0i=0, consider the commutative diagram with exact raws

where r′′r^{\prime\prime} is induced by rr and r′r^{\prime}. Since r′r^{\prime} is injective and rr is surjective, it follows that r′′r^{\prime\prime} is injective. Therefore 𝒞|H=0{\mathcal{C}}|_{H}=0.

We conclude that Z∩H=∅Z\cap H=\emptyset. Therefore dimZ≤0\dim Z\leq 0.

Step 2: We claim that ℍZ∗​(X,α){\mathbb{H}}^{*}_{Z}(X,\alpha) is an isomorphism. Indeed, denote U′=X′∖Σ′U^{\prime}=X^{\prime}\setminus\Sigma^{\prime}, U=X∖ΣU=X\setminus\Sigma. Then U′⊆X′U^{\prime}\subseteq X^{\prime} and U⊆XU\subseteq X are strict log smooth embeddings, and f:X′→Xf\colon X^{\prime}\to X maps U′U^{\prime} isomorphically onto UU. We compactify this data as in Corollary 1.12:

Since ff is proper, it is obtained from f¯\bar{f} by base change with the open embedding X⊆X¯X\subseteq\bar{X}. Denote Σ′¯=X′¯∖U′\bar{\Sigma^{\prime}}=\bar{X^{\prime}}\setminus U^{\prime}, Σ¯=X¯∖U\bar{\Sigma}=\bar{X}\setminus U. Consider the natural homomomorphism

Since the second square is cartesian, Σ′¯|X′=Σ′\bar{\Sigma^{\prime}}|_{X^{\prime}}=\Sigma^{\prime}, Σ¯|X=Σ\bar{\Sigma}|_{X}=\Sigma, and logarithmic sheaves commute with base change by open embeddings, we obtain an identification

From the quasi-isomorphism α¯|U¯​→∼​α|X∖Z\bar{\alpha}|_{\bar{U}}{\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}}\alpha|_{X\setminus Z}, we deduce that α¯\bar{\alpha} is a quasi-isomorphism over U¯\bar{U}. Therefore we obtain isomorphisms

Since ZZ is contained in the open subset XX of X¯\bar{X} and α¯|X=α\bar{\alpha}|_{X}=\alpha, it follows by excision that ℍZ∗​(X,α){\mathbb{H}}^{*}_{Z}(X,\alpha) is an isomorphism.

Step 3: Since dimZ=0\dim Z=0 and ℍZ∗​(X,α){\mathbb{H}}^{*}_{Z}(X,\alpha) is an isomorphism, Lemma 1.15 implies that α\alpha is a quasi-isomorphism. That is Z=∅Z=\emptyset, a contradiction. ∎

Corollary 1.18.

Let (X′,Σ′),(X,Σ)(X^{\prime},\Sigma^{\prime}),(X,\Sigma) be toroidal pairs, let f:X′→Xf\colon X^{\prime}\to X be a proper morphism such that f:X′∖Σ′→X∖Σf\colon X^{\prime}\setminus\Sigma^{\prime}\to X\setminus\Sigma is an isomorphism. Then for every pp, the natural homomorphism

ΩXp​(log⁡Σ)→R​f∗​ΩX′p​(log⁡Σ′)\Omega^{p}_{X}(\log\Sigma)\to Rf_{*}\Omega^{p}_{X^{\prime}}(\log\Sigma^{\prime})

is a quasi-isomorphism.

Proof.

We prove the claim in several steps.

Step 0: If moreover (X′,Σ′)(X^{\prime},\Sigma^{\prime}) is strict log smooth, if suffices to check the claim for a particular ff. Indeed, suppose g:(X′′,Σ′′)→(X,Σ)g\colon(X^{\prime\prime},\Sigma^{\prime\prime})\to(X,\Sigma) is another morphism with the same properties, with (X′′,Σ′′)(X^{\prime\prime},\Sigma^{\prime\prime}) strict log smooth, and we know the claim holds for gg. There exists a Hironaka hut

such that (X′′′,Σ′′′)(X^{\prime\prime\prime},\Sigma^{\prime\prime\prime}) is strict log smooth, and all arrows are isomorphisms above X∖ΣX\setminus\Sigma. The claim holds for X′′/XX^{\prime\prime}/X by assumption, and for X′′′/X′′X^{\prime\prime\prime}/X^{\prime\prime} by Theorem 1.17. Therefore it holds for X′′′/XX^{\prime\prime\prime}/X. By Theorem 1.17, it also holds for X′′′/X′X^{\prime\prime\prime}/X^{\prime}. Therefore it holds for X′/XX^{\prime}/X.

Step 1: Suppose (X′,Σ′),(X,Σ)(X^{\prime},\Sigma^{\prime}),(X,\Sigma) and ff are toric. In this case, ΩXp​(log⁡Σ)≃𝒪X⊕r\Omega^{p}_{X}(\log\Sigma)\simeq{\mathcal{O}}_{X}^{\oplus r} for some rr, and f∗​ΩXp​(log⁡Σ)→ΩX′p​(log⁡Σ′)f^{*}\Omega^{p}_{X}(\log\Sigma)\to\Omega^{p}_{X^{\prime}}(\log\Sigma^{\prime}) is an isomorphism. By the projection formula, our homomorphism is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if

𝒪X→R​f∗​𝒪X′{\mathcal{O}}_{X}\to Rf_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\prime}}

is a quasi-isomorphism. This holds, and can be proved combinatorially [3].

Step 2: Suppose (X′,Σ′)(X^{\prime},\Sigma^{\prime}) is strict log smooth and (X,Σ)(X,\Sigma) is toric. There exists a toric log resolution (X′′,Σ′′)→(X,Σ)(X^{\prime\prime},\Sigma^{\prime\prime})\to(X,\Sigma), which by construction is an isomorphism over the torus T=X∖ΣT=X\setminus\Sigma. Moreover, (X′′,Σ′′)(X^{\prime\prime},\Sigma^{\prime\prime}) is strict log smooth. By Step 1, the claim holds for X′′/XX^{\prime\prime}/X. By Step 0, it also holds for X′/XX^{\prime}/X.

Step 3: (X′,Σ′)(X^{\prime},\Sigma^{\prime}) is strict log smooth and (X,Σ)(X,\Sigma) is toroidal. The claim is local on XX. After possibly shrinking XX near a fixed point, there exists a hut

such that Y/XY/X and Y/ZY/Z are étale, ΣY\Sigma_{Y} is the preimage of both Σ\Sigma and ΣZ\Sigma_{Z}, and (Z,ΣZ)(Z,\Sigma_{Z}) is the restriction to an open subset of a toric pair. Our sheaves commute with étale base change, so our claim on XX is equivalent to the claim for the pullback of (X′,Σ′)→(X,Σ)(X^{\prime},\Sigma^{\prime})\to(X,\Sigma) to YY. On the other hand, we can construct a toric resolution, which when restricted to the open subset ZZ will satisfy the claim. After base change to YY, the claim still holds. We obtain two morphisms (Y′,Σ′)→(Y,ΣY)←(Y′′,Σ′′)(Y^{\prime},\Sigma^{\prime})\rightarrow(Y,\Sigma_{Y})\leftarrow(Y^{\prime\prime},\Sigma^{\prime\prime}) as in the claim, with (Y′,Σ′),(Y′′,Σ′′)(Y^{\prime},\Sigma^{\prime}),(Y^{\prime\prime},\Sigma^{\prime\prime}) strict log smooth. The claim holds for Y′′/YY^{\prime\prime}/Y. By Step 0, it also holds for Y′/YY^{\prime}/Y. Therefore it holds for X′/XX^{\prime}/X.

Step 4: By Hironaka, there exists a diagram

such that (X′′,Σ′′)(X^{\prime\prime},\Sigma^{\prime\prime}) is strict log smooth and X′′/X′X^{\prime\prime}/X^{\prime} is an isomorphism over X′∖Σ′X^{\prime}\setminus\Sigma^{\prime}. By Step 3, the claim holds for X′′/XX^{\prime\prime}/X and X′′/X′X^{\prime\prime}/X^{\prime}. Therefore it holds for X′/XX^{\prime}/X. ∎

2. Roots of sections

Let XX be a scheme and ℒ{\mathcal{L}} an invertible 𝒪X{\mathcal{O}}_{X}-module. For n∈ℤn\in{\mathbb{Z}}, denote the tensor product ℒ⊗n{\mathcal{L}}^{\otimes n} by ℒn{\mathcal{L}}^{n}.

Proposition 2.1.

Consider a global section s∈Γ⁡(X,ℒn)s\in\Gamma(X,{\mathcal{L}}^{n}), for some positive integer nn. Then there exist a morphism of schemes π:Y→X\pi\colon Y\to X and a global section t∈Γ⁡(Y,π∗​ℒ)t\in\Gamma(Y,\pi^{*}{\mathcal{L}}), such that tn=π∗​st^{n}=\pi^{*}s, and the following universal property holds: if g:Y′→Xg\colon Y^{\prime}\to X is a morphism of schemes, and s′∈Γ⁡(Y′,g∗​ℒ)s^{\prime}\in\Gamma(Y^{\prime},g^{*}{\mathcal{L}}) is a global section such that s′n=g∗​s{s^{\prime}}^{n}=g^{*}s, then there exists a unique morphism u:Y′→Yu\colon Y^{\prime}\to Y such that g=π∘ug=\pi\circ u and s′=u∗​ts^{\prime}=u^{*}t.

Proof.

Step 1: Suppose X=Spec⁡AX=\operatorname{Spec}A and ℒ=𝒪X{\mathcal{L}}={\mathcal{O}}_{X}. Then s∈Γ⁡(X,𝒪X)=As\in\Gamma(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{X})=A. The ring homomorphism

A→A⁡[T](Tn−s)A\to\frac{A[T]}{(T^{n}-s)}

induces a finite morphism π:Y→X\pi\colon Y\to X. If we denote by t∈Γ⁡(Y,𝒪Y)t\in\Gamma(Y,{\mathcal{O}}_{Y}) the class of TT, we have tn=π∗​st^{n}=\pi^{*}s. Let g:Y′→Xg\colon Y^{\prime}\to X be a morphism of schemes, and s′∈Γ⁡(Y′,𝒪Y′)s^{\prime}\in\Gamma(Y^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{Y^{\prime}}) with s′n=g∗​s{s^{\prime}}^{n}=g^{*}s. There exists a unique homomorphism of AA-algebras

A⁡[T](Tn−s)→Γ⁡(Y′,𝒪Y′)\frac{A[T]}{(T^{n}-s)}\to\Gamma(Y^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{Y^{\prime}})

which maps TT to s′s^{\prime}. This translates into a morphism u:Y′→Yu\colon Y^{\prime}\to Y with g=π∘ug=\pi\circ u and s′=u∗​ts^{\prime}=u^{*}t.

Step 2: Consider the 𝒪X{\mathcal{O}}_{X}-algebra 𝒜=⊕i=0n−1ℒ−i,{\mathcal{A}}=\oplus_{i=0}^{n-1}{\mathcal{L}}^{-i}, with the following multiplication: if ui,uju_{i},u_{j} are local sections of 𝒜i{\mathcal{A}}_{i} and 𝒜j{\mathcal{A}}_{j} respectively, their product is the local section ui⊗uju_{i}\otimes u_{j} of 𝒜i+j{\mathcal{A}}_{i+j} if i+j<ni+j<n, and the local section ui⊗uj⊗su_{i}\otimes u_{j}\otimes s of 𝒜i+j−n{\mathcal{A}}_{i+j-n} if i+j≥ni+j\geq n. Let π:Y=SpecX⁡(𝒜)→X\pi\colon Y=\operatorname{Spec}_{X}({\mathcal{A}})\to X be the induced finite morphism of schemes.

Let u∈Γ⁡(U,ℒ)u\in\Gamma(U,{\mathcal{L}}) be a nowhere zero section on some open subset U⊆XU\subseteq X. Then s|U=f​uns|_{U}=fu^{n} for some f∈Γ⁡(U,𝒪U)f\in\Gamma(U,{\mathcal{O}}_{U}). Then ℒ|U=𝒪U​u{\mathcal{L}}|_{U}={\mathcal{O}}_{U}u and 𝒜|U=⊕i=0n−1𝒪Uu−i{\mathcal{A}}|_{U}=\oplus_{i=0}^{n-1}{\mathcal{O}}_{U}u^{-i}, u−1∈Γ⁡(U,𝒜1)u^{-1}\in\Gamma(U,{\mathcal{A}}_{1}) satisfies (u−1)n=f(u^{-1})^{n}=f, and mapping T↦u−1T\mapsto u^{-1} induces an isomorphism over UU

π−1​(U)​→∼​SpecU​𝒪U​[T](Tn−f).\pi^{-1}(U){\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}}\operatorname{Spec}_{U}\frac{{\mathcal{O}}_{U}[T]}{(T^{n}-f)}.

Therefore the construction of 𝒜{\mathcal{A}} globalizes the local construction in Step 1.

Consider the section u−1⋅π∗​u∈Γ⁡(π−1​(U),π∗​ℒ)u^{-1}\cdot\pi^{*}u\in\Gamma(\pi^{-1}(U),\pi^{*}{\mathcal{L}}). It satisfies (u−1⋅π∗​u)n=π∗​(s|U)(u^{-1}\cdot\pi^{*}u)^{n}=\pi^{*}(s|_{U}). If u′u^{\prime} is another nowhere zero global section of ℒ|U{\mathcal{L}}|_{U}, then u′=v​uu^{\prime}=vu for some unit v∈Γ⁡(U,𝒪U×)v\in\Gamma(U,{\mathcal{O}}_{U}^{\times}). Since π∗​v=v\pi^{*}v=v, we obtain u′−1⋅π∗​u′=u−1⋅π∗​u{u^{\prime}}^{-1}\cdot\pi^{*}u^{\prime}=u^{-1}\cdot\pi^{*}u. So the section does not depend on the choice of uu. Since XX can be covered by affine open subsets which trivialize ℒ{\mathcal{L}}, it follows that u−1⋅π∗​uu^{-1}\cdot\pi^{*}u glue to a section tt of π∗​ℒ\pi^{*}{\mathcal{L}} whose nn-th power is π∗​s\pi^{*}s. The universal property can be checked on affine open subsets of XX on which ℒ{\mathcal{L}} is trivial, so it follows from Step 1. ∎

The morphism π:Y→X\pi\colon Y\to X, endowed with the section t∈Γ⁡(Y,π∗​ℒ)t\in\Gamma(Y,\pi^{*}{\mathcal{L}}), is unique up to an isomorphism over XX. It is called the nn-th root of ss. We denote YY by X⁡[sn]X[\sqrt[n]{s}], and tt by sn\sqrt[n]{s}.

Lemma 2.2.

Let s∈Γ⁡(X,ℒn)s\in\Gamma(X,{\mathcal{L}}^{n}) be a global section for some n≥1n\geq 1, let π:X⁡[sn]→X\pi\colon X[\sqrt[n]{s}]\to X be the nn-th root of ss. The following properties hold:

  • a)

    π∗𝒪X⁡[sn]=⊕i=0n−1ℒ−i\pi_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X[\sqrt[n]{s}]}=\oplus_{i=0}^{n-1}{\mathcal{L}}^{-i}.

  • b)

    Suppose the group of units Γ⁡(X,𝒪X∗)\Gamma(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{X}^{*}) contains a primitive nn-th root of 11. Then ℤ/n​ℤ{\mathbb{Z}}/n{\mathbb{Z}} acts on X⁡[sn]X[\sqrt[n]{s}], the morphism π\pi is the induced quotient map, and a) is the decomposition into eigensheaves.

  • c)

    The morphism π\pi is finite and flat.

  • d)

Proof.

All properties follow from the local description of the nn-th root in the case when XX is affine and ℒ=𝒪X{\mathcal{L}}={\mathcal{O}}_{X}. Note that π\pi is flat since ℒ{\mathcal{L}} is locally free. In b), let ζ∈Γ⁡(X,𝒪X∗)\zeta\in\Gamma(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{X}^{*}) be a primitive nn-th root of 11. The action is (ζ,a​Ti)↦ζi​a​Ti(\zeta,aT^{i})\mapsto\zeta^{i}aT^{i} for the local model in Step 1, and (ζ,ui)↦ζi​ui(\zeta,u_{i})\mapsto\zeta^{i}u_{i} for the global model in Step 2. ∎

Remark 2.4.

Let m,n≥1m,n\geq 1 and s∈Γ⁡(X,ℒm​n)s\in\Gamma(X,{\mathcal{L}}^{mn}). If ss vanishes nowhere and n∈Γ⁡(X,𝒪X∗)n\in\Gamma(X,{\mathcal{O}}^{*}_{X}), then X⁡[sn]→XX[\sqrt[n]{s}]\to X is a finite étale covering.

Remark 2.6.

2-B. Roots of units in a field

Let KK be a field. Let nn be a positive integer which is not divisible by the characteristic of KK. The polynomial Tn−1∈K⁡[T]T^{n}-1\in K[T] is separable. It has nn distinct roots in the algebraic closure of KK, denoted

μn​(K)={x∈K¯;xn=1}.\mu_{n}(K)=\{x\in\bar{K};x^{n}=1\}.

The multiplicative group μn​(K)\mu_{n}(K) must be cyclic, hence isomorphic to ℤ/n​ℤ{\mathbb{Z}}/n{\mathbb{Z}}. An nn-th root of unity ζ∈μn​(K)\zeta\in\mu_{n}(K) is a generator if and only if ζn/d≠1\zeta^{n/d}\neq 1 for every divisor 1<d|n1<d\mid n. A generator is called a primitive nn-th root of unity of KK. We have Tn−1=∏ζ∈μn​(K)(T−ζ)T^{n}-1=\prod_{\zeta\in\mu_{n}(K)}(T-\zeta) in K¯​[T]\bar{K}[T]. Therefore

Tn−xn=∏ζ∈μn​(K)(T−ζ​x)T^{n}-x^{n}=\prod_{\zeta\in\mu_{n}(K)}(T-\zeta x)

for every x∈K×x\in K^{\times}. If KK contains μn​(K)\mu_{n}(K), the decomposition holds in K⁡[T]K[T].

Let f∈K×f\in K^{\times}. Consider the integral extension K→K⁡[T]/(Tn−f)K\to K[T]/(T^{n}-f). We have

K[T]/(Tn−f)=⊕i=0n−1Kti.K[T]/(T^{n}-f)=\oplus_{i=0}^{n-1}Kt^{i}.
Lemma 2.12.

Under the isomorphism, this corresponds to the μd​(K)\mu_{d}(K)-action on the product given by the partial permutations ξ:(αζ)ζ↦(αξn′​ζ)ζ\xi\colon(\alpha_{\zeta})_{\zeta}\mapsto(\alpha_{\xi^{n^{\prime}}\zeta})_{\zeta}. 2-C. Irreducible components, normalization of roots

Lemma 2.15.

Let AA be an integral domain, integrally closed in its field of fractions QQ. Suppose QQ contains a root of T4+4T^{4}+4. Let 0≠a∈A0\neq a\in A and n≥1n\geq 1.

  • 1)

    Suppose Td−aT^{d}-a has no root in AA, for every divisor 1<d|n1<d\mid n. Then A⁡[T]/(Tn−a)A[T]/(T^{n}-a) is an integral domain with quotient field Q⁡[T]/(Tn−a)Q[T]/(T^{n}-a).

  • 2)

    Suppose char⁡(Q)∤n\operatorname{char}(Q)\nmid n, and AA contains μn​(Q)\mu_{n}(Q) and the reciprocal of the Vandermonde determinant associated to some ordering of the elements of μn​(Q)\mu_{n}(Q) (e.g. AA contains an algebraically closed field whose characteristic does not divide nn). Then the ring A⁡[T]/(Tn−a)A[T]/(T^{n}-a) has no nilpotents, and the integral closure in its total ring of fractions Q⁡[T]/(Tn−a)Q[T]/(T^{n}-a) is ⊕i=0n−1{q∈Q;qnai∈A}ti.\oplus_{i=0}^{n-1}\{q\in Q;q^{n}a^{i}\in A\}t^{i}.

Proof.

3. Normalized roots of rational functions

Let nn be a positive integer, let kk be an algebraically closed field which contains nn distinct roots of unity. We consider the category of normal kk-varieties and dominant morphisms. A morphism f:X→Yf\colon X\to Y is called dominant if for every irreducible component XiX_{i} of XX, f⁡(Xi)¯\overline{f(X_{i})} is an irreducible component of YY. A composition of dominant morphisms is again dominant. But the image of a dominant morphism may not be dense (e.g. the open embedding of a connected component).

Let X,YX,Y be normal kk-varieties. A dominant morphism f:X→Yf\colon X\to Y induces a pullback homomorphism of rings f∗:k⁡(Y)→k⁡(X)f^{*}\colon k(Y)\to k(X). It is compatible with composition of dominant morphisms, and maps invertible rational functions to invertible rational functions. Note that f∗f^{*} may not be injective.

Proposition 3.1.

Let X/kX/k be a normal variety, φ\varphi an invertible rational function on XX. Then there exists a normal variety Y/kY/k, a dominant morphism π:Y→X\pi\colon Y\to X and an invertible rational function tt on YY, such that tn=π∗​φt^{n}=\pi^{*}\varphi, and the following universal property holds: if Y′/kY^{\prime}/k is a normal variety, g:Y′→Xg\colon Y^{\prime}\to X is a dominant morphism, and t′t^{\prime} is an invertible rational function on Y′Y^{\prime} such that t′n=g∗​φ{t^{\prime}}^{n}=g^{*}\varphi, then there exists a unique dominant morphism u:Y′→Yu\colon Y^{\prime}\to Y such that g=π∘ug=\pi\circ u and t′=u∗​tt^{\prime}=u^{*}t.

Each factor is a integral domain, integrally closed in its function field. Therefore YY is normal. The morphism π\pi is dominant since it is finite. If we denote by t∈k⁡(Y)t\in k(Y) the class of TT, then tt is invertible and tn=π∗​φt^{n}=\pi^{*}\varphi.

Let Y′/kY^{\prime}/k be a normal variety, g:Y′→Xg\colon Y^{\prime}\to X a dominant morphism, and t′t^{\prime} an invertible rational function on Y′Y^{\prime} such that t′n=g∗​φ{t^{\prime}}^{n}=g^{*}\varphi. There exists a unique homomorphism of Q⁡(A)Q(A)-algebras

Q​(A)​[T](Tn−φ)→Q⁡(Y′)\frac{Q(A)[T]}{(T^{n}-\varphi)}\to Q(Y^{\prime})

which maps TT to t′t^{\prime}. Since AA maps to Γ⁡(Y′,𝒪Y′)\Gamma(Y^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{Y^{\prime}}), A¯\bar{A} maps to the integral closure of Γ⁡(Y′,𝒪Y′)\Gamma(Y^{\prime},{\mathcal{O}}_{Y^{\prime}}) in Q⁡(Y′)Q(Y^{\prime}). 𝒜(X,φ,n)=⊕i=0n−1𝒪X(⌊indiv(φ)⌋),{\mathcal{A}}(X,\varphi,n)=\oplus_{i=0}^{n-1}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}(\lfloor\frac{i}{n}\operatorname{div}(\varphi)\rfloor),

with the following multiplication: if ui,uju_{i},u_{j} are local sections of 𝒜i{\mathcal{A}}_{i} and 𝒜j{\mathcal{A}}_{j} respectively, their product is the rational function ui​uj∈𝒜i+ju_{i}u_{j}\in{\mathcal{A}}_{i+j} if i+j<ni+j<n, and ui​uj​φ∈𝒜i+j−nu_{i}u_{j}\varphi\in{\mathcal{A}}_{i+j-n} if i+j≥ni+j\geq n. Γ⁡(U,𝒜i)={ψ∈Q⁡(A);ψn​φi∈A}.\Gamma(U,{\mathcal{A}}_{i})=\{\psi\in Q(A);\psi^{n}\varphi^{i}\in A\}.

3-B. Toroidal criterion

Proposition 3.7.

With the notations of section 2-A, let X=TN​emb⁡(Δ)X=T_{N}\operatorname{emb}(\Delta) be a torus embedding. The torus character χv\chi^{v} becomes a rational function φ\varphi on XX.

  • a)

    Suppose n′=nn^{\prime}=n. Then the normalized nn-th root of φ\varphi is the toric morphism

    X′=TN′​emb⁡(Δ)→X=TN​emb⁡(Δ)X^{\prime}=T_{N^{\prime}}\operatorname{emb}(\Delta)\to X=T_{N}\operatorname{emb}(\Delta)

    induced by the inclusion N′⊆NN^{\prime}\subseteq N, endowed with the rational function χvn\chi^{\frac{v}{n}} on X′X^{\prime}.

  • b)

    Suppose kk contains μn\mu_{n}. Then the normalized nn-th root of φ\varphi has dd irreducible components, each of them isomorphic over XX to the toric morphism TN′​emb⁡(Δ)→TN​emb⁡(Δ),T_{N^{\prime}}\operatorname{emb}(\Delta)\to T_{N}\operatorname{emb}(\Delta), induced by the inclusion N′⊆NN^{\prime}\subseteq N.

Proof.

Let π:Y→X\pi\colon Y\to X be the normalized root of φ\varphi. Then π:π−1​(TN)→TN\pi\colon\pi^{-1}(T_{N})\to T_{N} is the normalized nn-th root of φ|TN\varphi|_{T_{N}}. Since φ|TN\varphi|_{T_{N}} is a unit, this coincides with the nn-th root of φ|TN\varphi|_{T_{N}}, which is described by Proposition 2.10. In case a), π−1​(TN)→TN\pi^{-1}(T_{N})\to T_{N} is isomorphic over TNT_{N} with TN′→TNT_{N^{\prime}}\to T_{N}. Therefore YY is the normalization of XX with respect to the field extension k⁡(TN)→k⁡(TN′)k(T_{N})\to k(T_{N^{\prime}}), which is exactly TN′​(emb⁡Δ)→TN​emb⁡(Δ)T_{N^{\prime}}(\operatorname{emb}\Delta)\to T_{N}\operatorname{emb}(\Delta). A similar argument works in case b), for each irreducible component of YY. ∎

Theorem 3.8.

Let kk be an algebraically closed field. Let U⊆XU\subseteq X be a quasi-smooth toroidal embedding defined over kk. Let φ\varphi be an invertible rational function on XX, let n≥1n\geq 1 such that char⁡k∤n\operatorname{char}k\nmid n. Let D=1n​div⁡(φ)D=\frac{1}{n}\operatorname{div}(\varphi), and suppose D|UD|_{U} has integer coefficients. Let π:Y→X\pi\colon Y\to X be the normalized nn-th root of φ\varphi. Then π−1​(U)⊆Y\pi^{-1}(U)\subseteq Y is a quasi-smooth toroidal embedding, and π\pi is a toroidal morphism.

Proof.

Let P∈XP\in X be a point. By Lemma 3.2.d), we may replace XX by an étale neighborhood of PP. By [1, Corollary 2.6], we may suppose there exists an étale morphism

τ:X→Z,\tau\colon X\to Z,

where Z=TN​emb⁡(σ)Z=T_{N}\operatorname{emb}(\sigma) is an affine torus embedding defined over kk, the cone σ\sigma is simplicial, and U=τ−1​(TN)U=\tau^{-1}(T_{N}). By [8], U⊆XU\subseteq X is a strict toroidal embedding.

Let D′D^{\prime} be the part of DD which is not supported by X∖UX\setminus U. It has integer coefficients, by assumption. By [7, Example 5.10], Cl⁡𝒪X,P\operatorname{Cl}{\mathcal{O}}_{X,P} is generated by the primes of X∖UX\setminus U passing through PP. Therefore there exists ψ∈k​(X)∗\psi\in k(X)^{*} such that div⁡(ψ)+D′\operatorname{div}(\psi)+D^{\prime} is zero on UU. Then div⁡(ψn​φ)\operatorname{div}(\psi^{n}\varphi) is supported by X∖UX\setminus U. By [8], there exists v∈N∗v\in N^{*} such that

div⁡(ψn​φ)=div⁡(π∗​χv).\operatorname{div}(\psi^{n}\varphi)=\operatorname{div}(\pi^{*}\chi^{v}).

That is u​ψn​φ=π∗​χvu\psi^{n}\varphi=\pi^{*}\chi^{v} for some unit uu. After the étale base change X⁡[un]→XX[\sqrt[n]{u}]\to X, we may suppose u=wnu=w^{n} for some unit ww. Therefore

(w​ψ)n​φ=π∗​χv.(w\psi)^{n}\varphi=\pi^{*}\chi^{v}.

By Lemma 3.7.b), the normalized nn-th root of χv\chi^{v} is a toroidal morphism. The total space is again quasi-smooth, since σ\sigma is simplicial. By étale base change, the normalized nn-th root of π∗​χv\pi^{*}\chi^{v} is also toroidal and quasi-smooth. By Lemma 3.3, the normalized nn-th root of (w​ψ)n​φ(w\psi)^{n}\varphi is isomorphic to the normalized nn-th root of φ\varphi. ∎

3-C. Comparison with roots of sections

Let X/kX/k be a normal variety.

Suppose f∈Γ⁡(X,𝒪X)f\in\Gamma(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{X}) does not divide zero. Then X⁡[f,n]X[f,n] coincides with the normalization of X⁡[fn]X[\sqrt[n]{f}] (root of regular function). If ff is a unit on XX, the root is already normal, and therefore X⁡[f,n]=X⁡[fn]X[f,n]=X[\sqrt[n]{f}].

Let φ\varphi be an invertible rational function on XX. Let V=X∖Supp⁡DV=X\setminus\operatorname{Supp}D be the (open dense) locus where φ\varphi is a unit. The restriction of X⁡[φ,n]→XX[\varphi,n]\to X to VV coincides with the nn-th root of the unit φ|V\varphi|_{V}. Therefore X⁡[φ,n]X[\varphi,n] is obtained by normalizing XX in the function field of each irreducible component of V⁡[φ|Vn]V[\sqrt[n]{\varphi|_{V}}].

Let ℒ{\mathcal{L}} be an invertible 𝒪X{\mathcal{O}}_{X}-module. Let s∈Γ⁡(X,ℒn)s\in\Gamma(X,{\mathcal{L}}^{n}) be non-zero. Choose an open dense subset U⊆XU\subseteq X such that ℒ|U{\mathcal{L}}|_{U} has a nowhere zero section uu. Let s|U=φ​uns|_{U}=\varphi u^{n} with φ∈Γ⁡(U,𝒪U)\varphi\in\Gamma(U,{\mathcal{O}}_{U}). Then the normalization of X⁡[sn]X[\sqrt[n]{s}] coincides with X⁡[φ,n]X[\varphi,n].

4. Index one covers of torsion divisors

Let kk be an algebraically closed field. Let X/kX/k be an irreducible, normal algebraic variety. Let DD be a ℚ{\mathbb{Q}}-Weil divisor on XX which is torsion, that is i​D∼0iD\sim 0 for some i≥1i\geq 1. The index of DD is

r=min⁡{i≥1;i​D∼0}.r=\min\{i\geq 1;iD\sim 0\}.

We suppose char⁡k∤r\operatorname{char}k\nmid r. Choose a non-zero rational function φ∈k​(X)×\varphi\in k(X)^{\times} such that div⁡(φ)=r​D\operatorname{div}(\varphi)=rD.

Lemma 4.1.

The polynomial Tr−φ∈k⁡(X)​[T]T^{r}-\varphi\in k(X)[T] is irreducible.

Proof.

We may apply Lemma 2.12. Suppose 1≤d|n1\leq d\mid n and Td−φT^{d}-\varphi has a root ψ∈K\psi\in K. Then div⁡(ψ)=rd​D\operatorname{div}(\psi)=\frac{r}{d}D, hence rd​D∼0\frac{r}{d}D\sim 0. The minimality of rr implies d=1d=1. ∎

We deduce that k⁡(X)​[T]/(Tr−φ)k(X)[T]/(T^{r}-\varphi) is a field, denoted k​(X)​(φr)k(X)(\sqrt[r]{\varphi}). The Kummer field extension

k​(X)⊂k​(X)​(φr)k(X)\subset k(X)(\sqrt[r]{\varphi})

has Galois group μr\mu_{r}. Let ψ\psi be a root of Tr−φT^{r}-\varphi in this extension. The Galois group action induces an eigenspace decomposition

k(X)(φr)=⊕i=0r−1k(X)⋅ψi.k(X)(\sqrt[r]{\varphi})=\oplus_{i=0}^{r-1}k(X)\cdot\psi^{i}.

Let π:Y→X\pi\colon Y\to X be the normalization of XX in the Kummer extension. By construction, Y/kY/k is an irreducible, normal algebraic variety with quotient field k​(X)​(φr)k(X)(\sqrt[r]{\varphi}). The root ψ\psi identifies with a rational function on YY such that ψr=π∗​φ\psi^{r}=\pi^{*}\varphi. In particular,

div⁡(ψ)=π∗​D.\operatorname{div}(\psi)=\pi^{*}D.

So π∗​D\pi^{*}D is linearly trivial on YY. The morphism π\pi is finite, determined as follows:

Lemma 4.2.

The Galois group μr\mu_{r} acts on YY relative to XX. The eigenspace decomposition is

π∗𝒪Y=⊕i=0r−1𝒪X(⌊iD⌋)⋅ψi.\pi_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{Y}=\oplus_{i=0}^{r-1}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}(\lfloor iD\rfloor)\cdot\psi^{i}.
Proof.

We have π∗𝒪Y=⊕i=0r−1ℱi⋅ψi\pi_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{Y}=\oplus_{i=0}^{r-1}{\mathcal{F}}_{i}\cdot\psi^{i} for some subspaces ℱi⊂k⁡(X){\mathcal{F}}_{i}\subset k(X). Locally on XX, a non-zero rational function a∈k​(X)×a\in k(X)^{\times} belongs to ℱi{\mathcal{F}}_{i} if and only if π∗​a⋅ψi∈𝒪Y\pi^{*}a\cdot\psi^{i}\in{\mathcal{O}}_{Y}. Since YY is normal, this is equivalent to div⁡(π∗​a)+i​π∗​D≥0\operatorname{div}(\pi^{*}a)+i\pi^{*}D\geq 0, that is div⁡(a)+i​D≥0\operatorname{div}(a)+iD\geq 0, or a∈𝒪X​(⌊i​D⌋)a\in{\mathcal{O}}_{X}(\lfloor iD\rfloor). Therefore ℱi=𝒪X​(⌊i​D⌋){\mathcal{F}}_{i}={\mathcal{O}}_{X}(\lfloor iD\rfloor). ∎

We deduce that (Y/X,ψ)(Y/X,\psi) is the normalized rr-th root of XX with respect to φ\varphi.

Call π:Y→X\pi\colon Y\to X the index one cover associated to the torsion ℚ{\mathbb{Q}}-divisor DD. It depends on the choice of φ\varphi. If φ1,φ2\varphi_{1},\varphi_{2} are two choices, they differ by a unit u∈Γ⁡(X,𝒪X×)u\in\Gamma(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{X}^{\times}), and the two associated morphisms Yi→X⁡(i=1,2)Y_{i}\to X\ (i=1,2) become isomorphic after base change with the étale covering X⁡[ur]→XX[\sqrt[r]{u}]\to X. If X/kX/k is proper, it follows that Yi→X⁡(i=1,2)Y_{i}\to X\ (i=1,2) are isomorphic, and therefore π\pi does not depend on the choice of φ\varphi.

Let D′=D+(f)D^{\prime}=D+(f). Then D′D^{\prime} is again torsion, of the same index. We have r​D′=(φ​fr)rD^{\prime}=(\varphi f^{r}) and (ψ​f)r=φ​fr(\psi f)^{r}=\varphi f^{r}. Therefore the Kummer field is the same, so Y→XY\to X is also an index one cover of D′D^{\prime}. In conclusion, for two linearly equivalent torsion ℚ{\mathbb{Q}}-divisors, one may choose isomorphic index one covers. In general, any two become isomorphic after an étale base change of XX (taking the rr-th root of some global unit).

Index one covers do not commute with restriction to open subsets, since the index may drop after restricting to an open subset.
